title: A Rivergate for the Trail
premise: Isandro Almeida has spent his life outrunning the shadow of his mother, famed archaeologist Dr. Vera Almeida, who vanished on the Rivergate coast eleven years ago and left him her field journals and a talent for reading ground he never wanted. When a storm tide uncovers a sea cave matching a legend she once dismissed, Isandro is coerced into joining a salvage expedition led by the man whose testimony closed her case. Following an underground river that only appears at certain tides, he discovers his mother survived, lived hidden among the cave's forgotten keepers, and traded her memory — and her name — for her life. Isandro must choose between dragging her back to a world that will consume her story and letting the river keep what it was paid, an ending that costs him his own certainty about who he is.
about_author: Ivo Kavanagh is the pen name of a former river guide turned writer who spent six seasons leading expeditions through coastal cave systems before a near-drowning ended that career. Kavanagh now writes adventure fiction from a houseboat, drawing on a private archive of tide charts, expedition logs, and stories guides tell after dark.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Isandro, working as a hired surveyor on the Rivergate coast, is summoned at dawn by a salvage crew whose storm-exposed cave matches a legend from his mother's journals. His POV establishes his bitterness and his uncanny instinct for reading terrain. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition — the past has surfaced, literally, and it has his mother's handwriting all over it.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed the Report
chapters.summary: Expedition backer Corvin Hale, the former rescue coordinator whose official report declared Vera Almeida dead, pressures Isandro aboard with money and veiled threats about his falsified survey licenses. Isandro agrees to guide them only as far as the cave mouth. Emotional beat: resentment hardening into resolve; Isandro tells himself he's in it for the money, and lies.

chapters.title: Marks in the Dark
chapters.summary: Inside the cave, Isandro finds survey marks cut in his mother's distinctive style — dated after her supposed death. The crew dismisses them as coincidence; Isandro cannot. A rising tide nearly traps the team, and only his reading of the water saves them. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into obsession; the dead don't leave fresh marks.

chapters.title: The River That Runs Both Ways
chapters.summary: The crew discovers the cave's river reverses with the tide, offering a passage inland that charts say shouldn't exist. Diver Teodora Reyes, the only crew member Isandro trusts, reveals Hale has been searching this coast for years and has buried two earlier expeditions' failures. Emotional beat: shifting alliances; Isandro realizes he is not the only one chasing something, and not the only one lying.

chapters.title: Keepers of the Source
chapters.summary: Following the river upstream at low tide, the team finds a hidden settlement's traces: tended stone channels, offerings, warnings carved in an old dialect — and one modern boot print, small, worn, familiar. Isandro's POV fractures between fieldwork discipline and hope he can't control. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear; someone alive is keeping this place, and knows they're coming.

chapters.title: The Price of the Passage
chapters.summary: A crew member, Grell, ignores the carved warnings and drowns in a sump when the tide turns early; the survivors realize the river enforces its own schedule and its own toll. Hale's mask slips — he knew the risks and spent Grell's life anyway. Emotional beat: the first true cost of the journey; Isandro confronts what survival has already made him willing to overlook.

chapters.title: A Woman Called Nothing
chapters.summary: Isandro, separated from the crew during a flood pulse, is found by the keepers and brought to their elder: a woman with his mother's hands and no memory of her name. Vera, hollowed by the bargain that bought her life, tends the river's source without knowing why. Emotional beat: devastating reunion without recognition — Isandro gets his mother back as a stranger, and must decide whether to tell her who she is.

chapters.title: What Vera Chose
chapters.summary: Through the keepers' accounts and Vera's buried field notes, the truth emerges: eleven years ago Vera discovered the river's source and its guardians, and the price of leaving with the knowledge was her memory of it — and of herself. Hale arrives with the remaining crew, armed, intent on taking the source by force. Emotional beat: the past fully revealed; Isandro understands his mother didn't abandon him — she paid so he would never be pulled into this. He was pulled in anyway.

chapters.title: The Turning of the Water
chapters.summary: Climax: Hale's crew breaches the source chamber; the river rises in answer, and Isandro must collapse the passage behind them — the only route out — to stop Hale, trapping everyone including himself and Vera. Teodora turns against Hale; Vera, moved by something older than memory, guides them through the keepers' flood channels as the chamber drowns. Hale, refusing to let go of his prize, is taken by the river. Emotional beat: sacrifice and reversal — the son saves the mother by trusting her instincts over his own.

chapters.title: A Rivergate for the Trail
chapters.summary: Isandro and Teodora lead Vera out through the estuary as the cave seals behind them. Vera remembers nothing of the river, but something in her settles; she asks Isandro his name, and he gives it — the first time he's claimed being her child out loud in a decade. He burns the survey marks' coordinates and writes his own account instead. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — identity is not what the river takes or the world records, but what you choose to carry forward.
